newsitem.title: CANADA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-U.S. LEAGUE AGREES TO PROP UP CANADIAN FOOTBALL LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-U.S. LEAGUE AGREES TO PROP UP CANADIAN FOOTBALL LEAGUE.

text.p: Four months after the Canadian Football League completed a chaotic season that many fans feared would be its last, the league on Wednesday made a life-saving deal with the National Football League.
The bigger and richer NFL will offer $3 million in loans to support the CFL's eight struggling clubs, which were mired in red ink last year.
"I'm delighted to announce what represents an exciting new chapter in the history of the Canadian Football League," CFL Chairman John Tory said in announcing the five-year deal.
Tory said the deal was the lifeline the CFL needed to keep its teams afloat after a dismal, money-losing 1996 season.
CFL Commissioner Larry Smith resigned last December after a failed U.S. expansion and the collapse of the 120-year-old Ottawa Rough Riders.
Tory said that "the majority of the franchises at the end of last year were financially unstable and the league itself was financially weakened after trying to support those unstable teams."
Officials of the two leagues said the NFL would also use its marketing muscle to help promote the Canadian game.
In return, NFL teams can cull CFL players for duty after the CFL Grey Cup championship game in late November.
Under the agreement, a CFL player could appear in Canada's championship game and then move to the NFL for the rest of its season, which runs through January.
Tory said the CFL was also in talks with the NFL to stage a "World Classic Bowl", which would pit the Grey Cup winner against the NFL-supported and European-based World League champion.
The agreement also allowed the NFL to stage regular season and exhibition games in Toronto and Vancouver.
NFL Commissioner Paul Tagliabue said the deal was part of his league's effort to expand football's global following.

"We want to see football succeed wherever it is played," Tagliabue said. "The CFL is an exciting brand of football with a rich history and a unique style of play. We believe a strong, vibrant CFL is very important to the sport."

Tagliabue said the agreement would not prevent the NFL from expanding into Canada, but he added there were no immediate plans to do so, especially with the NFL first commited to returning franchises to Los Angeles and Cleveland.
